section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence exchanged between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Treasury Department between October 1939 and January 1940. The documents concern reciprocal exemption from Federal income tax under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Japanese government officials and employees stationed in or visiting the United States. Individuals covered include naval inspectors and technical officers, university professors and researchers, financial commissioners, and staff of the Japan Association for the 1939-1940 New York World's Fair and Golden Gate International Exposition.

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. that Japan grants reciprocal income tax exemptions, recommending exemption for Takeo Kimura under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of note no. 247 dated October 10, 1939 from the Japanese Ambassador requesting Federal income tax exemption for Takeo Kimura. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that the Japanese Government grants reciprocal tax exemption to U.S. government employees in Japan performing similar services. The letter requests the Treasury Department take appropriate action.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Takeo Kimura
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the Japanese Ambassador's request for income tax exemption for Takeo Kimura and reports its referral to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Ambassador note no. 247 of October 10, 1939 regarding desired income tax exemption for Takeo Kimura, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Department of Naval Aeronautics. The note confirms that a copy of the request has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to exempting Kimura's official compensation from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Takeo Kimura

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of certification for Takeo Horiuchi and confirms instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes responds to the Secretary of State's letter of October 7, 1939 concerning the Federal income tax exemption of Takeo Horiuchi, who expects to sail from Seattle on October 13, 1939. Hanes acknowledges the State Department's certification of reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. He confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to the Internal Revenue officials concerned.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Response regarding Tax Exemption for Takeo Horiuchi

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Tadashi Nakayama, Assistant Professor at Osaka Imperial University visiting the Institute for Advanced Study.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Tadashi Nakayama, Assistant Professor at Osaka Imperial University residing at Fine Hall, Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey, be exempted from income taxes while in the United States. Nakayama was sent by the Japanese Government, derived his income solely from it, and arrived in San Francisco on September 3, 1937 on the Tatsuta Maru. The note states he is scheduled to depart San Francisco on November 23, 1939 on the same ship and asks that his name be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note requesting Tax Exemption for Tadashi Nakayama

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Assistant Professor Tadashi Nakayama.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Ambassador note no. 258 of October 19, 1939 regarding Tadashi Nakayama. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that the Japanese Government grants an equivalent tax exemption to U.S. government employees in Japan and that the character of services is similar. The letter notes Nakayama's planned departure from San Francisco on November 23, 1939 aboard the steamship Tatsuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Tadashi Nakayama
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 258 regarding tax exemption for Tadashi Nakayama and confirms its referral to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 258 of October 19, 1939 concerning the desired Federal income tax exemption of Tadashi Nakayama, Assistant Professor at Osaka Imperial University. The note acknowledges Nakayama's planned sailing from San Francisco on November 23, 1939 on the Tatsuta Maru. The Ambassador is informed that a copy of the note has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Tadashi Nakayama

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes confirms instructions will be issued regarding tax exemption for Takeo Kimura.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of October 17, 1939 enclosing a note regarding the tax exemption of Japanese national Takeo Kimura. Hanes notes the Secretary of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees. He confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Response regarding Tax Exemption for Takeo Kimura

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes confirms instructions will be issued regarding tax exemption for Tadashi Nakayama.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury

Hanes acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of October 25, 1939 regarding the tax exemption of Tadashi Nakayama, who expects to sail from San Francisco on November 23. Hanes acknowledges the certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding reciprocity. He confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Response regarding Tax Exemption for Tadashi Nakayama

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Yoshio Makino, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission in New York.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 287, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Yoshio Makino, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission at 120 Broadway, New York City, be granted income tax exemption while residing in the United States. Makino was sent by the Japanese Government, derived his income solely from it, and arrived in San Francisco on November 19, 1939 on the Tatsuta Maru. The Ambassador asks that Makino's name be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. government authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 287 requesting Tax Exemption for Yoshio Makino

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Yoshio Makino of the Japanese Financial Commission.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of the Japanese Embassy's note of December 7, 1939 concerning Yoshio Makino. Makino is identified as Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission in New York. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to U.S. government personnel and that the services performed are similar in character, recommending exemption from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Yoshio Makino
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 287 regarding tax exemption for Yoshio Makino and confirms referral to competent authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 287 of December 7, 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemption for Yoshio Makino, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission at New York. The Ambassador is informed that a copy of the note has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to granting the desired tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Yoshio Makino

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure and requests income tax exemption for Ichiro Kaifu, Manager of the Japan Association for International Expositions.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 292, the Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the departure of Ichiro Kaifu, Manager of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions, located at 2339 Lake Street, San Francisco. Kaifu derives his income solely from the Japanese Government and will leave San Francisco on January 4, 1940 aboard the steamship Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that his tax-exempt status be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 292 regarding Departure and Tax Exemption for Ichiro Kaifu

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Ichiro Kaifu prior to his departure.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of the Japanese Embassy's note of December 12, 1939 concerning Ichiro Kaifu. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to U.S. employees and that Kaifu's services are comparable in character. The letter notes Kaifu's planned departure from San Francisco on January 4, 1940 on the steamship Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Ichiro Kaifu
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 292 regarding tax exemption for Ichiro Kaifu and confirms referral to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 292 of December 12, 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemption for Ichiro Kaifu, Manager of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco World Fairs. The note recognizes Kaifu's impending sailing on January 4 from San Francisco on the Asama Maru. The Ambassador is advised that the request has been transmitted to the competent U.S. authority with a view to exempting Kaifu from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Ichiro Kaifu

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemptions for naval inspectors Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari in New York.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 294, the Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemptions for Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office, 1 Madison Avenue, New York City. Murata, Engine Construction Commander and Inspector of Construction and Ordnance, arrived in San Francisco on October 27, 1939 on the Asama Maru. Watari, Ordnance Commander, arrived in Seattle on November 9, 1939 on the Hikawa Maru. The Ambassador requests that their names be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 294 requesting Tax Exemption for Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for naval officers Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of the Japanese Embassy's note of December 14, 1939 regarding Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to U.S. government employees and that the services performed by the officers are similar in character. The letter requests the Treasury Department grant exemption on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that note no. 294 concerning Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari has been forwarded to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 294 of December 14, 1939 concerning Federal income tax exemption for Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari. Both officers are acknowledged as officials of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City. The Ambassador is informed that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Commander Toshio Murata and Commander Katsumi Watari

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes confirms that tax exemption instructions will be issued for Yoshio Makino.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.title: Treasury Department Response regarding Tax Exemption for Yoshio Makino

He confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to the relevant Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Response regarding Tax Exemption for Ichiro Kaifu

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure and requests income tax exemption for five Japanese exposition officials sailing from San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 305, the Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State of the departure and requests income tax exemption for five Japanese officials of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions, based in Bayside, Long Island. The named officials are Koichi Tennichi, Kichizo Higuchi, Fumio Kusumi, Yoshio Yeto, and Katsuo Kabe. Their income is derived solely from the Japanese Government, and they are scheduled to sail from San Francisco on January 18 aboard the steamship Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 305 regarding Departure and Tax Exemption for Officials of the Japan Association for International Expositions

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for five Japanese officials of the New York and Golden Gate expositions.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 305 of December 27, 1939 concerning officials of the Japan Association for the New York World's Fair and Golden Gate International Exposition. The officials are scheduled to sail from San Francisco on January 18 on the Tatuta Maru. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions and that the services performed are similar in character.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Japanese Exposition Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 305 regarding tax exemption for Japanese exposition officials and confirms transmission to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 305 of December 27, 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemption for officials of the Japan Association for the New York World's Fair and the Golden Gate International Exposition. The note acknowledges that the officials are sailing from San Francisco on January 18 on the steamship Tatuta Maru. The Ambassador is informed that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Exposition Officials

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 306, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics, be granted income tax exemption while in the United States. Koike serves as an official of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office, 1 Madison Avenue, New York City, and arrived in Seattle on December 15, 1939 aboard the Heian Maru. The Ambassador requests that his status be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 306 requesting Tax Exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 306 of December 28, 1939 concerning Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike. Koike is identified as Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to U.S. employees and that the services performed are similar in character, recommending exemption from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 306 regarding tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike and confirms referral to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 306 of December 28, 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. The note confirms that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to exempting Koike from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure and requests income tax exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: In note no. 307, the Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State of the departure and requests income tax exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. Shiraishi is stationed at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office, 1 Madison Avenue, New York City, and derives his income solely from the Japanese Government. He will leave San Francisco on January 18, 1940 aboard the steamship Tatuta Maru, and the Ambassador asks that his name be brought to the attention of competent U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 307 regarding Departure and Tax Exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of the Japanese Embassy's note of December 28, 1939 concerning Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi. Shiraishi is identified as Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics, sailing from San Francisco on January 18, 1940 on the Tatuta Maru. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to U.S. personnel and that the services performed are similar in character.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 307 regarding tax exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi and confirms transmission to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 307 of December 28, 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. The note acknowledges Shiraishi's scheduled departure from San Francisco on January 18, 1940 aboard the steamship Tatuta Maru. The Ambassador is informed that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi
